newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gold closes lower in Hong Kong in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Gold closes lower in Hong Kong in quiet trade.

text.p: Gold closed lower on Wednesday after mild selling interest in the Asia, extending the decline in New York overnight, but dealers said trade was quiet in the absence of Japanese traders who were on holiday.
"No one wants to take any positions in this nervous market," said a dealer at an international metals house.
Bullion ended at US$353.00/50 an ounce, down from New York's $353.70/354.20 close on Tuesday and Hong Kong's previous close at $356.80/357.30.
"Gold is likely to fall towards US$350 levels as central banks and producers continue to heighten bearish sentiment," a dealer said.
Local gold ended HK$31 lower at HK$3,266 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange society dropped to +0.01 from +0.50.
